title: Interviewer shadow rotation and evidence archive protocol
content:
Purpose:
This protocol defines a lightweight, repeatable process for rotating interviewers through a "shadow" track, capturing primary evidence from live interviews, and curating an immutable evidence archive to support more consistent hiring decisions and fairness audits. It balances operational overhead with signal quality: aim is high-signal artifacts (candidate work samples, scored rubrics, interviewer notes) with a small, searchable index for post-hire calibration and compliance.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all full-cycle interviewers across engineering, product, and platform teams.
- Mandatory for interviewers hired or promoted after Jan 2025 within their first 90 days of taking interview panels.
- Recommended cadence for senior interviewers: once per quarter shadow rotation to surface drift and surface calibration gaps.

Goals (success metrics):
- Reduce inter-interviewer variance on role rubric scores by 15% within 6 months (measured on paired candidate re-evals).
- Achieve 95% completeness on evidence capture fields for hiring panel decisions.
- Provide an auditable evidence snapshot for 100% of offers and 90% of declines for audit windows.

Core components:
1) Shadow rotation: design
   - Pairing: one interviewer (shadow) is assigned to observe a live interview run by a primary interviewer. The shadow sits muted and does not interact unless pre-approved (e.g., take a clarifying question).
   - Rotation length: typical rotation is 4 interviews or 2 calendar weeks, whichever comes first.
   - Roles: "Primary" (runs the interview), "Shadow" (observes and records evidence), "Coordinator" (schedules and ensures evidence ingestion).

2) Evidence capture template (required fields)
   - Candidate ID (internal): string
   - Role & level: e.g., SWE-II
   - Interview focus: system design / coding / culture fit / oncall-sre
   - Time-stamped rubric scores (0-4 scale) by dimension (technical execution, communication, problem decomposition, ownership)
   - Freeform observation notes (3–5 bullet max)
   - Red flags / pass-signals checklist (checkbox shortlist)
   - Recording link or timestamped transcript location (if recorded; follow privacy consent rules)
   - Shadower calibration note: one sentence about disagreement points (if any)
   - Confidence level: low/medium/high (shadower)
   - Submission timestamp + submitter name

3) Archive storage & naming conventions
   - Location: Google Drive evidence archive (shared_drives/company/misc/interview-evidence-archive)
content_addendum:
- File name format: candidate_{YYYYMMDD}_{ROLE}_{CANDIDATEID}_{INTERVIEWTYPE}_{PRIMARYINITIALS}.pdf or .txt
   - Always include a JSON metadata sidecar with the required fields (example templates in Confluence)

Operational rules and privacy:
- Consent: Candidate consent for recording must be obtained and documented before any audio/video is captured. If a candidate declines recording, the shadow still submits notes but marks recording=false.
- Access: Evidence archive read permissions: people-ops, hiring manager, and legal by default. Long-term access requires approval.
- Retention: Evidence for declined offers: retain 2 years; for hired candidates keep 5 years per compliance table (exceptions handled by legal).

Interviewer shadow checklist (what the shadow does live):
- Before interview: review role rubric + shortlist key dimensions (2 minutes)
- During: take structured notes aligned to rubric dimensions (one line per dimension). Note timestamps for notable moments.
- Immediately after (within 24h): submit artifact using submission template. Include confidence rating and a 1-line calibration note if your score differs more than 1 point from primary.

Post-rotation calibration ritual (for each rotation cohort):
- Weekly sync: 30 minutes with 3–4 paired interviewers and a people-ops facilitator to review 2 anonymized evidence packets. Focus on one dimension (e.g., "problem decomposition") and compare scoring rationale.
- Mini-calibration doc: each sync produces a 1-page micro-retro capturing 3 takeaways and 2 action items (upload to evidence archive under /calibrations).

Scoring normalization guidelines (quick rules):
- Adopt a rubric anchor: provide example clips/snippets for 0, 2, 4 per dimension on Confluence. Use these as reference during rotations.
- Disagreement escalation: if shadower and primary differ >1 point on hire/no-hire signal, tag "needs-review" and add to next calibration meeting.

Quality checks and enforcement:
- Completeness gate: interviews without a submitted evidence packet are flagged by the coordinator and the primary's interviewing privileges are temporarily limited after 3 missed submissions in 60 days until training is completed.
- Audit sample: people-ops runs a monthly sample (5% of interviews) checking for rubric adherence and presence of calibration notes.

Onboarding pathway for new interviewers (first 90 days):
- Week 0: mandatory quickstart doc and rubric read (must ack in HR LMS).
- Week 1–4: shadow rotation paired with senior interviewer (2 weeks minimum).
- Week 4–8: co-interview for two panels (co-run with senior) and solo under observation for 2 panels.
- Week 8–12: independent interviews with quarterly shadow requirement activated. People-ops issues final certification token after passing a calibration check.

Exception handling and edge cases:
- Expedite hiring windows: for urgent roles, coordinators may run an "expedited shadow" where evidence is captured but the shadow participates in question time; all expedited cases must be documented and tagged.
- External panels: for third-party interviewers (agencies/advisors), require at least one people-ops observer and a recorded rubric to be accepted into the archive.

Operational templates (quick links and minimal copy):
- Submission template (one-line): https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/HR/Interview+Evidence+Template
- Calibration examples: https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/HR/Rubric+Anchors
- Training module: PEOPLE-342 (LMS enrollment required)

Next steps for pilot (Q1-Q2 rollout):
1) Pilot with Eng Platform and People Ops partner squads (6-week pilot). Recruit 12 interviewers, run rotations, collect evidence.
2) Run three calibration meetings and measure variance on the 2 anchor dimensions.
3) Iterate templates and auto-checks based on pilot pain points.

Notes to reviewers (what we need feedback on):
- Is rotation length (4 interviews / 2 weeks) the right tradeoff?
- Are the required evidence fields minimal enough to avoid submission fatigue?
- Permission model: does the default access list feel permissive/overly restrictive?

Appendix — quick exemplar (anonymized):
- CandidateID: C-20240701-513
- Role: SWE-II
- Interview focus: backend-coding
- Rubric: Tech Exec 3, Communication 2, Decomp 3, Ownership 2
- Notes: "asked to optimize naive two-pointer; candidate refactored and identified edge-cases; struggled to explain tradeoffs under pressure"
- Shadower note: "primary emphasized asymptotic reasoning more; I would probe earlier for edge-cases"
- Confidence: medium
